newsitem.title: USA: Hartford Whalers hockey to leave Conn - report.
newsitem.headline: Hartford Whalers hockey to leave Conn - report.

text.p: The Hartford Whalers rejected Connecticut Gov. John Rowland's proposal to build a $150 million arena and will leave the state at the end of this season, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
Rowland will hold a news conference on the Whalers at 1100 EST Wednesday.
The National Hockey League team is expected to pay the state more than $5 million as part of an exit agreement, the Courant said, citing unnamed sources.
The payment will be made because the team is being allowed to leave one year early under its contract with the state.
The main stumbling block was the team's concern about losing about $45 million during the three years it would have taken to build a new arena.
Rowland and the Whalers had been negotiating for several months.
Among the cities that have been mentioned as possible new homes for the Whalers are Minneapolis/St. Paul; Columbus, Ohio, and Nashville.
